summary: The note outlines a set of upcoming community initiatives for substance abuse prevention and recovery, rolling out from November 2023 to May 2024. They span school education, public campaigns, recovery centers, law enforcement training, medical provider workshops, workplace programs, free Narcan access and a mobile app. The central theme is that no one battles addiction alone and that education, support, enforcement and medical care must work together.
one_line: A local health series details prevention and recovery initiatives from November 2023 to May 2024, from school curricula to Narcan access and a sobriety app.
key_facts: Dr. Maria Lopez, Director of the County Health Department, said at an October 15, 2023 meeting that substance abuse affects students, professionals and the unemployed alike.
The 'Healthy Choices Curriculum' enters county middle school programs starting November 1, 2023, led by Dr. Kevin Turner, a specialist in adolescent psychology.
The Healthy Choices Curriculum uses interactive modules on the effects of drugs and alcohol and teaches refusal skills and strategies for coping with peer pressure.

Public service campaigns conceived by marketing expert Janet Clarke launch in December 2023 with the tagline 'Your Life, Your Choice – Say No To Substance Abuse', using billboards, local radio and social media.
The 'Pathway to Recovery' initiative, led by Dr. John Carter, will open new recovery centers on January 5, 2024, offering counseling, support groups and structured recovery programs.
Pathway to Recovery includes a volunteer program in which former addicts mentor people currently in recovery.

Law enforcement training sessions begin in February 2024 to teach officers to handle substance-related incidents more empathetically and identify people needing intervention, per Police Chief Roberto Garcia.

From March 15, 2024, medical professionals countywide will attend workshops on screening for early signs of substance abuse and discussing prescription drug misuse risks, led by primary care physician Dr. Susan Park.

Local businesses are launching workplace wellness programs with confidential counseling, educational seminars and treatment referrals, with Human Resources consultant Michael Thompson driving dialogue between employers and employees.
Narcan, an emergency treatment for suspected opioid overdoses, will be available free at strategic community locations from April 2024 through pharmacies and first responders.
The 'Stay Sober' mobile app, developed by local startup SoberTech, is expected to go live in May 2024 with support group connections, counselor appointment scheduling and recovery goal tracking.
